paper_findings: For alpha > 0 the proof's appeal to [brunswic2021cauchy, Section 1.2] for 'J^pm(p) is the closure of its interior' (l.1480-1482) is not needed: Z^mp(E_alpha) = E_alpha, and J^pm(p) = closure I^pm(p) follows from the vertical time shift (Static.closure_Iplus). The citation is needed only for kappa = 0.

ETT.tex:1480-1482: the cited fact 'for every p the set J^±(p) is the closure of its interior' is false for J⁻(p) at a BTZ point of E₀: there J⁻(p) is the half-line {r = 0, τ ≤ τ(p)}, with empty interior (e0_Jminus_axis_ne_closure_interior). This already contradicts defi:causal_E0 itself (l.1347 gives that half-line), so the finding stands whatever OQ-34 rules. The fact holds for J⁺(p) at every point and for J⁻(p) off the axis (e0_Jplus_eq_closure_interior, e0_Jminus_eq_closure_interior).

ETT.tex:1480-1491, one proof-level repair (the statement is unchanged). The condition 'if p ∈ Z^∓(E_κ)' (l.1482) lets the J⁻ case reach BTZ points (Z⁺(E₀) = E₀), where J⁻(p) ≠ closure I⁻(p) = ∅ (e0_Jminus_axis_ne_closure_Iminus); statement (b) excludes them, so it is the proof that overreaches. The paragraph for (a) at BTZ points (l.1488-1491) argues from I⁺(p) = reg(J⁺(p)), false at every BTZ point (DEC-64; E0.Iplus_ne_Jplus_diff), though (a) holds there (e0_densite_a). A repair: take p ∈ Z^±(E_κ) at l.1482, restrict the cited fact of l.1481 to the points where it holds, adjust l.1488 and delete l.1488-1491; with Z^± the main argument covers (a) at BTZ points too. It is not a misprint: the printed Z^∓ fits l.1488, and it is why l.1488-1491 exist.

At κ = 0 the closure-of-interior fact is not needed: push-up, Z⁺ = E₀, Z⁻ = reg(E₀) and the closedness of J^±(p) suffice (for (b), with an axis step: the axis points just below an axis point q of J⁻(p) are ≪ p when p is regular (E0.lt_axis_iff), and they tend to q). The closedness of J^±(p) is stated nowhere in the paper and would come from the same description of the cones in [brunswic2021cauchy, §1.2]: an observation, not an error.

statements.label: def:singular_spacetime
statements.title: Singular flat spacetime
statements.scope_notes: Abstracted as SingularFlatSpacetime: SingularFlatAxioms (the causal facts the paper derives for E≥0-manifolds, each citing its line) plus connectedness; witnessed on the timelike line. (WP-11, audited) T-ett-port-e0-sfa (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (a checklist row is a reading; the earlier witnesses also include every connected T2 second-countable flat manifold, sing = ∅; fixed at graduation): the first witness with sing₀ ≠ ∅, E₀ (Causal.E0.singularFlatAxioms, sing₀ = axis; Causal.E0.exists_singularFlatSpacetime_sing_zero_nonempty), a verbatim port of gx's BTZ causality (144 constants, elaborated types checked). It rests on the readings of E₀ (OQ-34, OQ-35) and on reading the definition as not requiring every model X_α. Also at E₀, unmarked: globallyHyperbolic, and the abstract lem:past_BTZ, cor:K_injectif, prop:K_densite_sing, cor:K_ordre, geroch_hypotheses_of_singularFlat. T-ett-e0-gx-structure (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (two findings reworded, a redundant rigidity theorem dropped, the group reading added to the checklist; fixed at graduation): E₀ as a singular (Flat.isom 2, Minkowski 2)-manifold under DEC-25 (Causal/Port/E0GXStructure.lean, E0GX.singularGX): the sector atlas (isAEAtlas_sectorAtlas), holonomy hol(2π) parabolic (isParabolic_holLin_two_pi), single powers on overlap components, Reg = E₀ ∖ axis (reg_eq; no chart meets the axis, source_inter_axis_eq_empty), Sing = axis; the model-free lemma chartIso_of_mem_maximalAEAtlas_of_agreeOn and corollaries; hreg at κ = 0 (chartIso_of_mem_aeAtlas) and (b′) at regular sources. Roadmap (not the paper): the evidence of T-ett-e0-gx-structure, point (3), states as [r] a model-free lemma ('if every chart of an a.e. atlas A of Y is a ChartIso DY DX, G acts by strong morphisms and DY is absolutely minimal, then every chart of maximalAEAtlas A is a ChartIso'). It is false. Causal.AESupportCounterexample.counterexample, on C with the translations: DX = rightward horizontal segments, DY = the same segments avoiding 0, both absolutely minimal on every open set; the identity of C minus {0} is a chart isomorphism generating an a.e. atlas; the identity of C is in its maximal atlas but is not a chart isomorphism (-1 <= 1 in DX, not in DY). The true form needs the maximal atlas to have the generating support, or DY to agree with the model at the extra points. T-ett-ealpha-gx-structure plans to reuse this lemma. At alpha = 2pi the maximal atlas covers the line, so that target must use chartIso_of_mem_maximalAEAtlas_of_agreeOn and supply the agreement on the line. T-ett-maxatlas-hoist (master, 2026-11-21): the model-free section, the counterexample and the two restated gx lemmas are hoisted into Causal/MaximalAEAtlasIso.lean under their full names (the gx lemmas now Causal.isPreconnected_ball_diff_zero, Causal.isPortly_ne_zero; E0GX.* deprecated aliases). T-ett-singular-sfa (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (a duplicated generic lemma disclosed, findings routed to notes, the empty-locus question recorded as a reading; fixed at graduation), Causal/Port/SFAManifolds.lean: the definition implies the library's abstraction. Setting: every Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold (DEC-25: SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M) and every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point (IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over massAModelCausality). There C.SingularFlatAxioms (SFALocal.sing M) holds with no field left (singularFlatAxioms, one application of SFABTZ.singularFlatAxioms_iff_lines to SFALine.line and SFAMassiveLine.massive_line), mixed manifolds included. On a connected M it is a SingularFlatSpacetime, and only then (singularFlatSpacetime, singularFlatSpacetime_iff). The natural causality (OQ-18: IsAtlasCausalityDEC25 with MassACovered M) is one such causality (singularFlatAxioms_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25, singularFlatSpacetime_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). It exists, and it is the only absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point (exists_singularFlatAxioms, exists_singularFlatSpacetime, through EModelsBPrime.massA_causalite_models). Sub-families: E₀-manifolds (singularFlatSpacetime_e0, A = {0}) and E_{>0}-manifolds (singularFlatSpacetime_of_massive, A = (0, ∞); a special case of singularFlatSpacetime). Witnesses with a singular point, each conclusion out of these theorems: E₀ (sing₀ = axis; nonvacuous_e0, nonvacuous_e0_natural, nonvacuous_e0Manifold) and E_π (sing_π = the line; nonvacuous_epi, nonvacuous_epi_massive; E_κ is connected, massive_connectedSpace). No witness has points of both kinds. Hypotheses: E^{1,2}_A-manifold with A = ℝ₊ → read (DEC-25: MassACovered, implied by the cover); a general A ⊆ ℝ₊ → not stated (special case A = ℝ₊, with A = {0} and A = (0, ∞)); connected → carried by the SingularFlatSpacetime forms only; Hausdorff, second countable → carried (RamcovGX.tex:474, DEC-25); the causality generated by the X_A-atlas → read (OQ-18), weakened in the main forms to any absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point; E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82). Empty singular locus: ETT is silent. gx's def:atlas (RamcovGX.tex:1905-1917, DEC-25) does not require every α ∈ A to occur (« an X_α-chart for some α ∈ A »). Its « X_A-atlas … covering M », read literally, forces sing(M) ≠ ∅ for M ≠ ∅; the library reads it as covering Sing(M) (MassACovered; GXSingularDEC25 checklist, ⚠ weakened). Every theorem here holds in either reading, and E₀ and E_π satisfy the literal one, so no OQ is opened. Roadmap (not the paper): the generic lemma preconnectedSpace_of_geodesicSpace duplicates staticCausality.preconnectedSpace_of_geodesic (Causal/LemmaKBare.lean:600) for pseudometric spaces; it is a hoist candidate for Causal/Static.lean.

paper_findings: ETT.tex:1331-1333 writes sing(E_alpha) for the singular line and reg(E_alpha) for its complement, an (Isom(E),E)-manifold. Read through DEC-25, sing(E_0) is the singular locus of the singular (G,X)-structure only if the (Isom(E),E)-structure does not extend across the line. That holds: the holonomy of a loop about the line is the parabolic isometry hol(2pi), which is not the identity (Causal.E0GX.source_inter_axis_eq_empty, reg_eq). ETT.tex:1331 asserts it (« its singular locus {r=0} is a lightlike line »), and l.1322–1324 give blanket sources, but without an argument or the precise reference l.1324 promises; one sentence would do.

ETT.tex:1502, « connected »: nothing Section 3 derives for singular flat spacetimes uses it. Every field of SingularFlatAxioms holds at every Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold with its natural causality, connected or not (Causal.SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms). The abstraction adds connectedness only (singularFlatSpacetime_iff), and no theorem of the library under SingularFlatSpacetime uses that field. The statements of Section 3.3 written for « a singular flat spacetime » therefore hold for every E≥0-manifold, as prop:K_calcul (l.1557) and prop:mesure_admissible (l.1726) are already stated. Section 4 states « connected » again where it wants it (l.1933). The definition may stay as it is.

paper_findings: The reason for DEC-18. As printed (no strong causality), the remark overclaims: theo:geroch asks local causal convexity and a pair of admissible measures, and prop:mesure_admissible gives the measures only for strongly causal M; nothing in Section 3 makes a singular flat spacetime strongly causal (l.1216 reads 'locally causally convex => strongly causal'). By hand, not formalized (no E_alpha in the library): for alpha > 0, E_alpha modulo a translation along its timelike singular line is a connected singular flat spacetime with a non-empty singular locus (so the example does not depend on whether A = R_+ allows an empty one); its singular line closes into a closed timelike curve, it is totally vicious (J^-(q) = M for every q), and it carries no measure admissible in the past (property 3 fails). E^{1,2} modulo a timelike translation is the same example if an empty singular locus is allowed. None of (i)-(iii) holds there, so theo:geroch_sing without strong causality is not refuted, but its proof (l.1781-1785) needs strong causality for (ii)=>(iii) and (iii)=>(i). The example is local (not a kb/0014 artefact). Since line/massive_line ask the closed embedding only when M is causal, the structure does not exclude such a quotient. Under DEC-18 the remark and theo:geroch_sing assume M strongly causal.
J^±(p) ≠ {p} (l.1783-1785) follows abstractly: I^±(p) is non-empty and open (or J^-(p) accumulates at p at a BTZ point) and M has no isolated point; the '3-dimensional J^+(p)' is not needed.

paper_findings: ETT.tex:1529–1530, « By Property prop:GX_sing_dec it is a connected 1-dimensional submanifold; since M is a differential manifold, it is parametrisable by ℝ »: this misses a compact component, a circle, which is not parametrisable by ℝ as a line (no closed embedding ℝ → ℝ/Pℤ exists, Causal.LineDevelopment.not_isClosedEmbedding_circle). Such a component occurs only when M is not causal, since in a causal M a locally injective causal curve over ℝ is injective (injective_of_isCausal). def:singular_spacetime allows it, e.g. E₀ or E_κ modulo a translation along the singular line (by hand, not formalized). The statement of (a) survives under DEC-6, since a causal curve need not be injective: the component is then the image of a periodic, inextensible causal curve, as on the circle (circle_isLineDevelopment, circle_line). Suggested wording: « it is the image of a continuous, locally injective map ℝ → M, periodic when Δ is compact and an embedding when M is causal ».

ETT.tex:1530, « since M is a differential manifold, it is parametrisable by ℝ »: the step is the classification of connected 1-manifolds (ℝ or the circle), which is not cited. It needs Hausdorff and second countability, which M has as a manifold; the long line shows that the countability is used. The formalization does without the classification and without second countability. The charts of E₀ and E_κ make the transitions along the line translations, and the development of the line (Causal.LineDevelopment.exists_development) needs only M Hausdorff and Δ closed. At α = 0 the translations come from brunswic2021cauchy prop:isom at α = β = 0 (BTZ_1.tex:378–384): near the axis, two X_A-charts at a BTZ point differ by a rotation about the axis after a translation along it (Causal.BPrimeE0.exists_eqOn_rotE0_tauShift). With the development, this gives (a) at α = 0 at every Hausdorff E≥0-manifold (Causal.SFALine.line). A citation of the classification, or of prop:isom together with the development argument, would close the step. At α > 0 the same replacement holds. The X_A-charts into E_κ make sing_κ(M) a translation line, because two of them differ near the line by a translation along it after a rotation about it (brunswic2021cauchy prop:isom, α = β > 0, in local form; Causal.BPrimeEAlpha.prop_isom_local, used in Causal.SFAMassiveLine.isTranslationAtlas). So a citation of prop:isom at l.1530 closes the step for every α ∈ ℝ₊, with Hausdorff alone. The same fact supplies the orientation that l.1531–1533 leave implicit: « locally chronal » yields « a chronal curve » for a parametrisation that is future-directed in every chart, and the transitions never reverse the chart time.

paper_findings: The proof l.1640-1690 can be replaced by three lines, given I^+(p) = J^+(p) \ sing_0 at BTZ points in its global form (the field Iplus_eq): every point is strongly tarentin in the future, so push-up gives J^+(x) in closure I^+(x) = closure K^+(x); in the past a regular y <= x is strongly tarentin in the past (push-up again), a BTZ y <= x with x regular has y << x by I^+(y) = J^+(y) \ sing_0, and at a BTZ x the half-line accumulates at x. Strong causality and lem:densite_modele (l.1464) are not needed. Causal arc-connectedness is unneeded only because Iplus_eq is assumed globally: the paper states it in the model (l.1352), and deriving the global form in M is the chart plus causal arc-connectedness argument of l.1663-1669.

DEC-64: the identity I^+(p) = J^+(p) \ sing_0 used in the shortcut above is false in E_0 (defi:causal_E0); the shortcut survives with the true form (Iplus_of_lt): a BTZ y <= x with x regular is the limit of the points u_n < y of its BTZ line (lem:past_BTZ / SingularPastAt), each u_n << x, so y lies in the closure of I^-(x). Causal arc-connectedness is now used (u_n ∈ sing_0, via lem:past_BTZ (b)); strong causality and lem:densite_modele are still not needed. At M (T-ett-singular-rows): DEC-64's global field is a theorem at every E≥0-manifold (Causal.SFABTZ.Iplus_of_lt). So « strongly causal » can be dropped from the statement of l.1634 itself (Causal.SingularRowsK.K_densite_sing_local, which needs no Hausdorff axiom or second countability either). The paper's proof uses strong causality for chart neighbourhoods causally convex in M (l.1659–1660, l.1665–1666, l.1677–1678, l.1683–1684); the formalization reads one chart at a time and needs none.

paper_findings: ETT.tex:1716, « Let M be a causal E≥0-manifold »: the conclusion does not need « causal ». Read property 3 of defi:mesure_dieckmann with p < q meaning p ≤ q and p ≠ q, as the paper uses it at l.1275. Then a causality carrying a measure admissible in the past, or in the future, is causal: for x ≤ y ≤ x with x ≠ y the set J⁻(y) ∖ J⁻(x) is empty, so property 3 fails (Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.isCausal_of_admissiblePast, isCausal_of_admissibleFuture; model-free). Hence the remark holds at every Hausdorff E≥0-manifold with a BTZ point (mesure_unilaterale). The computation uses causality for the segment ]p, q], so the word may stay. The totally vicious example behind DEC-18 (rem:singular_flat_spacetime_therefore) is an instance.

statements.scope_notes: From prop:mesure_dieckmann_topo with the local measures as a named hypothesis; asks only causality. (WP-11, audited) T-ett-measures-e0 (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (a docstring nit, stale texts, the finding's rewording; fixed at graduation), Causal/Port/MeasuresE0.lean: the measures of the proof at E₀, the first instance with sing₀ ≠ ∅. The sentence l.1737-1741 as printed: λ₃ satisfies properties 1., 3., 4. in the future (lam3_future), λ₃ + λ₁ (λ₁ Lebesgue measure on the axis) in the past (lam3_add_lam1_past); of 1., 3., 4. each fails exactly one on the other side (lam3_past_profile: λ₃ property 3. in the past; lam3_add_lam1_future_profile: λ₃ + λ₁ property 4. in the future). E0.modelMeasures (U = E₀, as timelikeLine_modelMeasures) and E0.mesure_admissible; the paper's local form, λ₃ + λ₁ and λ₃ restricted to a relatively compact causally convex U_p in every neighbourhood, is paper_measures_local. The planner's route checked in every step (chronological rays r ↦ (u + r, re^{iθ}), the λ₃-preserving shear, polar coordinates, at most one axis point in J⁻(A) ∖ K⁻(A)); Measure.toFinite in place of a Gaussian weighting. Hypotheses: every E≥0-manifold → strengthened (M = E₀); E₀ → read (OQ-34, OQ-35); causality → carried (E0.isCausal). The reading of λ₃ (« the Lebesgue measure of ℝ³ », l.1737) and λ₁ (l.1739) on E₀ is settled by the class result: every finite measure with the null sets of λ₃ (resp. λ₃ + λ₁) is admissible in the future (resp. past) (admissibleFuture_of_equiv, admissiblePast_of_equiv; admissible*On_restrict_of), and every plausible reading (Cartesian dτ dx dy, the coordinate measure dτ dr dθ, any parametrisation of the axis) has those null sets; no OQ. T-ett-measures-ealpha (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (routing of findings, a checklist label, stale blocked_on; fixed at graduation), Causal/Model/MeasuresEAlpha.lean: the measures of the proof at E_κ, κ > 0 (massive κ = staticCausality (Cone κ)). The sentence l.1736-1737 as printed, λ₃ read as dt ⊗ dr dθ in the cylindrical coordinates (MeasuresEAlpha.lam3): λ₃ satisfies properties 1., 3., 4. in the past (lam3_past) and in the future (lam3_future). It is infinite (lam3_univ), hence the restriction to a relatively compact U_p (l.1741), where λ₃ restricted is admissible on both sides (lam3_admissibleOn; paper_measures_local: such a U_p in every neighbourhood of every point). One finite measure, muE κ = (lam3 κ).toFinite, is admissible in the past and in the future at once (exists_admissible_past_future). Hence MeasuresEAlpha.modelMeasures (U = E_κ, as E0.modelMeasures) and MeasuresEAlpha.mesure_admissible, the proposition's conclusion at E_κ, proved directly: E_κ has no SingularFlatAxioms witness yet (T-ett-singular-sfa). Static layer, for every static ℝ × X: Minkowski's reduction verbatim (static_mesure_dieckmann_of); null frontiers of every ≪-past or ≪-future set for dt ⊗ ν, ν any s-finite measure (static_prod_frontier_of_past, _of_future, by vertical sections); the class result and restriction to causally convex open sets (static_admissible_of_equiv, static_admissiblePastOn_restrict_of, static_admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of); property 3's local form (static_pos_past_inter, static_pos_future_inter; kb/0148). Hypotheses: every E≥0-manifold → strengthened (M = E_κ); strong causality → used only in its open form by paper_measures_local (massive_stronglyCausalOpen); μ₋, μ₊ → carried, stronger (one measure for both). A massive singular line is no obstruction to admissibility in both senses, consistent with rem:mesure_unilaterale, whose obstruction needs a BTZ line. The reading of λ₃ on E_κ (no Cartesian coordinates for κ ≠ 2π) is settled by the class result, as at E₀. dt dr dθ, the Riemannian dt ⊗ r dr dθ (lam3Riem_equiv) and the chart pull-back (2π/κ) dt ⊗ r dr dθ have the same null sets. Every finite measure in that class is admissible on both sides (admissible_of_equiv, admissible_of_equiv_riem), as is every restriction to a causally convex open set (admissiblePastOn_restrict_of, admissibleFutureOn_restrict_of); no OQ. Roadmap note, not a paper finding: the planner's polar image of a measure on all of ℝ × ℝ/κℤ charges the apex (map_polar_apex_pos), so its product with dt is not in the class of λ₃ (not_absolutelyContinuous_map_polar). It is admissible nonetheless (exists_admissible_charging_singLine): properties 1.-4. do not determine the null-set class. T-ett-measures-manifolds (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (the cut diamond's relative compactness misdescribed, the two findings on l.1742-1743 merged into one wording, non-findings rerouted, the transfer split into the ETT layer; fixed at graduation), Causal/Remarks/MeasuresManifolds.lean (transfer: Causal/MeasureTransfer.lean). Hypothesis (i) of the proof, ModelMeasures, now holds at every strongly causal E≥0-manifold (DEC-7's StronglyCausal), for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point (IsoChartsCoverDEC25 over MassAModel, any G, any singular structures of the models: massA_modelMeasures; the natural one: massA_modelMeasures_of_natural). It holds in local form, inside every neighbourhood (ModelMeasuresLocal, massA_modelMeasuresLocal). At E₀-manifolds with their natural causality: e0Manifold_modelMeasures. Hence the proposition at every such manifold satisfying SingularFlatAxioms (massA_mesure_admissible: the strict SingularFlatAxioms.mesure_admissible with ModelMeasures discharged and strong causality in place of causality). At every Hausdorff, second countable, strongly causal E₀-manifold it follows from the three BTZ fields (e0Manifold_mesure_admissible). Route: the model's causally convex set U′ is chosen first, inside φ(V), where V ⊆ the chart source is causally convex in M. U = φ⁻¹(U′) is then causally convex in M (ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage, by causal arc-connectedness, le_of_causallyConvexIn_of_subset). The model measure on U′ is carried back through the chart, which needs no convexity (ChartIso.admissiblePastOn; J⁻ and K⁻ transport ChartIso.symm_mem_Jminus_iff, symm_mem_Kminus_iff, from mem_Kminus_of_intertwine). Model side: E0.modelMeasures_local and MeasuresEAlpha.modelMeasures_local; on E^{1,2} a finite measure in the class of λ₃, restricted. Hypotheses: E≥0-manifold → read (DEC-25, OQ-18), and SingularFlatAxioms for the conclusion → strengthened; strongly causal → carried (DEC-7; StronglyCausalOpen is not used on M); Hausdorff → weakened to R1Space M for ModelMeasures (regularity of the measure carried back); relatively compact U_p → weakened (U_p inside every neighbourhood); causal arc-connectedness → discharged (massA_dec25_models_of_isoChartsCover, SFALocalE0.causallyArcConnected). Witnesses with a singular point: e0_nonvacuous (every hypothesis of massA_mesure_admissible at E₀, and its conclusion), e0Manifold_nonvacuous, epi_nonvacuous (ModelMeasures at E_π). Family instances instMeasurableSpaceMassAModel and instBorelSpaceMassAModel, by cases on o: rfl to E₀'s ℝ × ℂ and to E_κ's ℝ × Cone κ (MeasuresEAlpha.instMeasurableSpaceCone). They do not fire at a fixed model and create no diamond. No second σ-algebra on Cone κ. T-ett-singular-sfa (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (fixed at graduation), Causal/Port/SFAManifolds.lean: the proposition holds with no hypothesis left beyond the readings at every strongly causal (DEC-7), Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold with its natural causality, connected or not, mixed ones included (mesure_admissible_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). It holds for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point (mesure_admissible: MeasuresManifolds.massA_mesure_admissible fed with SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms). At E₀-manifolds: MeasuresManifolds.e0Manifold_mesure_admissible_natural. Witnesses with a singular point: E₀ (nonvacuous_e0, nonvacuous_e0_natural, nonvacuous_e0Manifold) and E_π (nonvacuous_epi). Hypotheses: E≥0-manifold → read (DEC-25, OQ-18), weakened in mesure_admissible; strongly causal → carried; Hausdorff, second countable → carried (RamcovGX.tex:474, DEC-25); a measure → carried, Borel ([MeasurableSpace M] [BorelSpace M]); E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82). The two proof-level findings on l.1734-1743 stand; no new finding.

paper_findings: ETT.tex:1742-1743, proof-level: « Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p » holds for property 4 (restriction_convexe, Causal/ArcConnected.lean) but not for bare property 3, which asks the mass of J⁻(q) ∖ J⁻(p) (resp. J⁺(p) ∖ J⁺(q)) to lie inside U_p. It does for the paper's measures, and for every measure in their class, because that set meets every neighbourhood of q (resp. p) in a non-empty open set or, in the past at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line (pos_past_inter, pos_future_inter). The bare inference fails (by hand, not formalized): on Minkowski space a finite measure equivalent to λ₃ restricted to {t < −1} is admissible in the past and vanishes on every U_p inside {t > −1}. Suggested wording: « … turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p, since J⁻(q) ∖ J⁻(p) (resp. J⁺(p) ∖ J⁺(q)) meets every neighbourhood of q (resp. p) in a non-empty open set or, in the past at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line ». At E_κ, κ > 0, the local form holds for every measure positive on non-empty open sets (Causal.MeasuresEAlpha.static_pos_past_inter, static_pos_future_inter).

ETT.tex:1734-1743, proof-level, distinct from the property-3 finding above. That one is about what lem:restriction_convexe delivers once the set is causally convex in the model; this one is about whether it is. « Strong causality provides a relatively compact open neighbourhood U_p of p, causally convex in M and contained in a chart with model E_κ », then « Lemma restriction_convexe turns properties 3 and 4 of the model into properties 3 and 4 of U_p ». Applied in the model, the lemma needs φ(U_p) causally convex in E_κ, and U_p causally convex in M does not give it. Lean witness: Causal.MeasuresManifolds.cutDiamond_separates. Take M = E^{1,2} ∖ {(0,0)}, the chart the inclusion (a chart isomorphism), and U_p the open diamond I((−2,0),(2,0)) with its centre removed. U_p is open, inside the chart and causally convex in M, with compact closure in E^{1,2}. Its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}, since (0,0) lies between (−1,0) and (1,0). That U_p is not relatively compact in M, because its closure in M misses the centre. The paper's relative compactness does not save the step (by hand, not formalized). Take M = E^{1,2} ∖ K, with K the closed disc {t = 0, |x| ≤ 3}, and U_p the union of the open diamonds I((−1.1,0),(−0.9,0)) and I((0.9,0),(1.1,0)). U_p is open, relatively compact in M and inside the chart (the inclusion). It is causally convex in M: no causal curve of M joins the two diamonds, because one would cross t = 0 at |x| < 1.2. Its image is not causally convex in E^{1,2}, again because (0,0) lies between (−1,0) and (1,0). The proposition is not affected. Choose U′ causally convex in the model first and put U_p = φ⁻¹(U′), which is causally convex in M by strong causality and causal arc-connectedness of M (ChartIso.causallyConvexIn_source_inter_preimage). The chart carries the measure back with no convexity (ChartIso.admissiblePastOn). Suggested wording for l.1734-1743, which also takes in the property-3 finding above: « Strong causality provides a neighbourhood V of p, causally convex in M and contained in a chart φ with model E_κ. Let U′ ⊂ φ(V) be a relatively compact open neighbourhood of φ(p), causally convex in E_κ, and U_p = φ^{-1}(U′). Since V is causally convex in M and M is causally arc-connected, x ≤ y ≤ z in M with x, z ∈ U_p gives φ(x) ≤ φ(y) ≤ φ(z) in E_κ, so U_p is causally convex in M. [...] Restricted to the relatively compact U′ these measures are finite, so property 2 holds too. Lemma restriction_convexe turns property 4 of the model into property 4 of U′. Property 3 holds on U′ since J⁻(q) ∖ J⁻(p) (resp. J⁺(p) ∖ J⁺(q)) meets every neighbourhood of q (resp. p) in a non-empty open set or, in the past at a BTZ point, in a segment of the singular line. The chart φ carries properties 1 to 4 from U′ to U_p. »

statements.scope_notes: Strongly causal (DEC-18). The equivalence rests only on theo:geroch's cited step; the Σ × ℝ splitting is proved from the flow of lem:vecteur as a named hypothesis (its openness is asserted, not argued, by the paper). (WP-11, audited) T-ett-geroch-iii-i (atlas-team, 2026-11-20), audit AUDIT-1 minor (wording, fixed in round 1). The formalized statement (SingularGeroch.geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal) is false: chronological Minkowski space with an empty singular locus satisfies SingularFlatAxioms, strong causality and ModelMeasures (Causal.not_geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal, sorry-free); the paper's theorem is not refuted (OQ-33). Not an anchor of this row. T-ett-singular-rows-geroch (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor (fixed at graduation), Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsGeroch.lean; the equivalence is in the scaffold remainder CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGeroch. The results are stated at M itself, for every absolutely minimal causality with an isomorphic chart at each point, the natural one included. (i)⇒(ii) and (i)⇒(iii) hold at every Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold with no hypothesis left (geroch_sing_i_imp_ii, geroch_sing_i_imp_iii and their _of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 forms). There SingularFlatAxioms comes from SFAManifolds.singularFlatAxioms, ModelMeasures from MeasuresManifolds.massA_modelMeasures, and strong causality from global hyperbolicity (stronglyCausal_of_globallyHyperbolic). Connectedness and strong causality are not used in these two directions. (ii)⇒(iii) holds at every strongly causal one (geroch_sing_ii_imp_iii). The splitting holds at every connected causal one given VecteurFlow (geroch_sing_split). The equivalence at connected, strongly causal E≥0-manifolds is stated (CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing, geroch_sing_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25) and rests only on geroch_sing_iii_imp_i (OQ-32). OQ-33's witness, chronological Minkowski space, does not satisfy its hypotheses: it has an isomorphic chart at no point (by hand, not formalized). VecteurFlow had no witness at E₀ before T-ett-geroch-split-flow (below). At a BTZ point the orbit of lem:vecteur's X is null (l.1756), so the chronal-flow splitting (HasChronalCausalFlow.nonempty_isCauchySplitting) does not apply there; only IsCausalFlow.exists_isCauchySplitting could, given J^±(S) closed. Witnesses: E₀ (nonvacuous_e0_geroch, nonvacuous_e0_natural) and E_π (nonvacuous_epi_geroch). Hypotheses: singular flat spacetime → read (DEC-25, OQ-18); connected → carried by the equivalence and the splitting, weakened elsewhere; strongly causal → carried (DEC-18) by (ii)⇒(iii) and the equivalence, weakened in (i)⇒(ii) and (i)⇒(iii); the measures → discharged; (ii) → read (DEC-15); (iii) → read (DEC-14); « homeomorphic to Σ × ℝ » → strengthened (VecteurFlow); E₀ and Isom(E^{1,2}) → read (OQ-34, OQ-35; OQ-82). T-ett-geroch-split-flow (atlas-team, 2026-11-22), audit AUDIT-1 minor (docstring wording at graduation: imports no model directly, no chronal causal flow; the l.1763 finding names OQ-34), Causal/SingularSplitting.lean and Causal/Remarks/SingularRowsSplitting.lean, sorry-free, unmarked: the « Moreover » (l.1778–1796) from any causal flow φ (IsCausalFlow: a continuous ℝ-action whose orbits are inextensible future causal curves, with no fixed point; the C⁰ content of lem:vecteur's flow) and any Cauchy surface S: ψ(x, t) = φ_t(x) is a homeomorphism S × ℝ ≃ₜ M and a Cauchy splitting, at every causal SingularFlatAxioms spacetime (SingularFlatAxioms.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow; J^±(S) closed from sigma_separe_of_isCausal) and at every causal, Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold (SingularRowsSplitting.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow; natural causality, rows_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). No global hyperbolicity, connectedness or openness hypothesis: VecteurFlow's openness field (l.1792, asserted) is a theorem (isOpenMap_of_vecteurFlow), and at a causal SingularFlatAxioms spacetime VecteurFlow and IsCausalFlow are equivalent (nonempty_vecteurFlow_iff). At E₀ the τ-translation is a causal flow (isCausalFlow_tauFlow), null and not chronal (not_lt_tauFlow), VecteurFlow is inhabited (vecteurFlow_e0) and geroch_sing_split is instantiated (nonvacuous_e0, nonvacuous_e0_natural). No singular flat spacetime with a BTZ point has a chronal causal flow (SingularFlatAxioms.not_hasChronalCausalFlow), so the chronal-flow splitting never applies there. lem:vecteur itself, a causal flow at every E≥0-manifold, is not formalized. Unmarked: OQ-32 (the equivalence), readings OQ-18, OQ-34, OQ-35, OQ-82.

paper_findings: See rem:singular_flat_spacetime_therefore: the proof's 'direct consequence of theo:geroch and prop:mesure_admissible' needs strong causality, which, without DEC-18, is available only in direction (i)=>(ii)/(iii). The E_alpha-modulo-a-translation example is the reason for DEC-18. The former paper-form geroch_sing and its tagged sorry stronglyCausal_of_ii_or_iii are removed; no form without strong causality is stated.

The formalized statement of theo:geroch_sing is false: CausalScaffold.SingularGeroch's geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal (SingularFlatAxioms, strong causality, ModelMeasures ⇒ TFAE[(i),(ii),(iii)]). Witness: chronological Minkowski space with an empty singular locus (Causal.not_geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal, sorry-free). A throwaway check derived False from geroch_sing_of_stronglyCausal with it. This refutes the abstraction, not the paper. ETT.tex:1781 'a direct consequence of Theorem theo:geroch' inherits the gap of theo:geroch's (iii)⇒(i). A true singular flat spacetime may still satisfy the theorem through the local closedness of its model relations (lem:densite_modele, ETT.tex:1464), which SingularFlatAxioms does not carry. Stated at genuine E≥0-manifolds (IsoChartsCoverDEC25; CausalScaffold.SingularRowsGerochEquiv: Causal.SingularRowsGeroch.geroch_sing), the theorem is out of this witness's reach. Chronological Minkowski space has an isomorphic chart at no point, for any singular structure. By hand: a chart isomorphism carries ≤_U and ≪_U onto a model's; every non-empty open set of a model contains x ≤ y with x ≠ y and not x ≪ y; and the reflexive chronological causality has no such pair. Not formalized.

ETT.tex:1792 (T-ett-geroch-split-flow): « ψ is a local diffeomorphism » needs Σ a smooth hypersurface transverse to X, while Σ is only a topological Cauchy surface. Topologically the step is J^±(Σ) closed, which the paper derives afterwards from ψ (l.2067, l.2079) but which holds without ψ (lem:Sigma_separe's « In particular », Causal.SingularRowsCauchy.sigma_separe_of_isCausal). With it the « Moreover » holds for any causal flow: no C¹, no transversality, no global hyperbolicity, no connectedness (Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.geroch_sing_split_of_isCausalFlow).

ETT.tex:1763 (T-ett-geroch-split-flow; not an error, the paper says « future causal »): at E₀, read under OQ-34 (the metric −2dτdr + dr² + r²dθ²; under the printed −dτ² + dr² + r²dθ², ∂_τ is timelike), the vertical field's flow is null at every point, not only on the singular line (Causal.SingularRowsSplitting.not_lt_tauFlow), and no flow of a singular flat spacetime with a BTZ point is chronal (Causal.Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.not_hasChronalCausalFlow), so the classical « a timelike flow closes J^±(Σ) » argument is unavailable as soon as there is a BTZ point.

paper_findings: The reason for DEC-19, formalized (Causal/Port/CupCapBTZCounterexample.lean): lem:cup_cap_BTZ as printed (M strongly causal, ETT.tex:1825–1829) is false. Witness: M = E_0 ∖ {w}, w = (0,0) on the BTZ line, with the structure pulled back along the inclusion (opensSingularGXStructure, DEC-25) and its natural causality C (unique, absolutely minimal, causal; by MassAModelsInstance.massA_dec25_e0_manifolds also the natural causality over the whole family E_{≥0}). M is a connected, Hausdorff, second countable E_0-manifold, a singular flat spacetime (SingularFlatSpacetime, sing_0(M) the punctured axis), strongly causal in DEC-7's form and with open neighbourhoods. Causal.CupCapBTZCounterexample.not_cupCapBTZAsPrinted proves ¬ C.CupCapBTZAsPrinted (SFALocalE0.sing M), the strict Prop itself (packaged: exists_counterexample, not_forall_cupCapBTZAsPrinted). Data: p = (1,0) ∈ sing_0(M); p_n = (1, 1/(n+1)) → p, regular, with p ∉ J^-(p_n); z = (−1,0). Then z << p_n for every n: the straight chronal segment from z to p_n meets the axis only at z, so it avoids w. Meanwhile J^-(p) = ]w,p] (Jminus_p). So z, and with it the whole half-line of the axis below w (halfLine_subset_diff), lies in ⋃_N ⋂_{n≥N} J^-(p_n) and not in J^-(p) ∖ {p}. No proviso is left: E_0's strong causality is proved (E0.stronglyCausal) and carried to every open subset, and p ∈ Int J^+(z) is not used. What fails is the closedness of J^+(z) (not_isClosed_Jplus_z), the hypothesis of cup_cap_BTZ_of_isClosed; M is not globally hyperbolic (not_globallyHyperbolic). So the proof 'as for lem:J_int' (l.1832) cannot work. That proof (l.1805–1809) reduces to a chart at p causally convex in M, while the inclusion ⊂ needs z ≤ p_n ⇒ z ≤ p for z outside every such chart, a global property strong causality does not give. The witness is a singular flat spacetime of the paper in the library's readings of E_0 (OQ-34, OQ-35), of its causality (OQ-18) and of the group (OQ-82). Its only use (l.2122) is in a globally hyperbolic setting, where it holds: under DEC-19 the lemma is stated for globally hyperbolic M, its certificate cupCapBTZAsPrinted_of_globallyHyperbolic unchanged, and the printed strongly causal form stays the Prop Causal.Causality.CupCapBTZAsPrinted, now refuted. The certificate is instantiated at a BTZ point of E_0, its antecedents holding (Causal.SingularRowsK.nonvacuous_e0_certificate): at p = (0,0), with p_n = (−1/(n+1), 0) → p along the axis from below, p ∉ J^-(p_n) and ⋃_N ⋂_{n≥N} J^-(p_n) = J^-(p) ∖ {p} ≠ ∅ (nonvacuous_e0_cup_cap). So the printed form holds at E_0, which is globally hyperbolic, and fails at E_0 ∖ {w}.

paper_findings: ETT.tex:1940-1941: 'The map M → A∩B is a Cauchy embedding, so φ(Σ) is a Cauchy surface of A∩B' is asserted without argument. That φ(Σ) meets each causal curve of A∩B at most once is proved (eq_of_mem_image_inter); that it meets every inextensible curve of A∩B is the open step. In the Lorentzian case it holds by an end-point argument (the future end points of the two extensions coincide and would lie in (A∖B) ∩ (B∖A)).

ETT.tex:1941-1942: 'every point of A∩B lies on an inextensible causal curve' — the existence of inextensible causal curves through every point is proved nowhere (GerochEquiv's SCOPE notes the same gap); carried as a model fact.

ETT.tex:1939-1940: the appeal to theo:geroch_sing (M homeomorphic to Sigma x R, to make Sigma connected) is not needed. A ∩ B contains the connected set phi(M), and every point of A ∩ B lies on an inextensible causal curve of A ∩ B meeting phi(Sigma) ⊆ phi(M) (ett_c_ext_connexe_curves, ETT.tex:1941-1942), so A ∩ B is connected for any Cauchy surface Sigma (c_ext_connexe_of_connectedSpace). Suggest: 'every point of A ∩ B is joined inside A ∩ B to the connected set phi(M)'.

ETT.tex:1940-1941: 'the map M -> A ∩ B is a Cauchy embedding, so phi(Sigma) is a Cauchy surface of A ∩ B' is not needed for the conclusion, and it stays unproved even over the geometry. Proved: phi(Sigma) meets every causal curve at most once (ett_c_ext_connexe_curves), and A ∩ B is causally convex in N and globally hyperbolic (ett_c_ext_connexe_convex). The existence half needs an inextensible curve of A ∩ B to lie, through a reparametrisation, on inextensible curves of A and of B. The abstract form (exists_mem_image_inf) is neither proved nor refuted (SubExtensionAbstract SCOPE).

ETT.tex:1960-1961: 'Thus (∧, φ) ∈ ℰ' needs that the inclusion of i₁(M₀) into the union ∧ is a Cauchy embedding (global hyperbolicity of ∧ and the Cauchy property of i₁(Σ₀) in ∧), which does not follow from the same facts for each M; it is not argued.

ETT.tex:1960-1965: the proof gives more than the statement, and it is proved: the maximal common sub-extension receives a unique morphism from every common sub-extension (ett_cauchy_pgcd), and every maximal one has image the union of ℰ in M1 (ett_cauchy_pgcd_range). Suggest stating it as 'a greatest common sub-extension', which makes 'unique up to equivalence' immediate. The two gaps already recorded for this row are about the paper's text, which still argues neither point: φ is not shown injective (ETT.tex:1953-1960), and the union is not shown Cauchy-included (ETT.tex:1960-1961). Over the geometry both are proved from interface fields: A2 timeFunction (Sbierski Lemma 3.3) gives IsCGHD.injOn, and A2 curvesExtend with causal arc-connectedness gives isCGHD_mcghd. Their E₀ discharge is owed (T-ett-cbg-e0). The recorded paper_findings stay.

ETT.tex:1945-1949, abstract reading (not the paper's setting, DEC-60): the scaffold's abstract statement (CausalScaffold.SubExtension.cauchy_pgcd: abstract 𝕄≥0-morphisms, rigidity as the causal IsRigid) is false for non-local causalities. (a) not_cauchyPgcdAbstract refutes it as formalized. The witness on ℝ has two causalities that agree on every open set of diameter < 1 and are not absolutely minimal (not_absolutelyMinimalOn_witness), and rigidity holds (bigCausality_isRigid). Of two maximal common sub-extensions, bigSub is not Equivalent to the base. The converse DOES hold (base_equivalent_bigSub: a bijective morphism whose inverse is not one). So (a) rests on the library's Equivalent being directional, and under the paper's symmetric 'equivalent' (ETT.tex:1927-1928) those two ARE equivalent. (b) cauchyPgcdAbstract_counterexample_symm refutes it under every reading of 'equivalent' that asks for a morphism between the two: directional, one-step symmetric, isomorphism. In the same setting, two maximal common sub-extensions (ℝ, C', id, id, id) and (ℝ, C'', id, id, id), with C', C'' incomparable between C₀ and C₁, admit no morphism in either direction. (c) NOT refuted: the equivalence relation generated by bijective morphisms. Here i₁ = id is bijective, so the base maps bijectively onto every common sub-extension (via Y.a), and the two witnesses are equivalent through the base (kernel-checked by the AUDIT-2 probe, not stated in the files). Abstractly the one-step symmetric relation is not transitive, and this witness shows it: base ~ C', base ~ C'', C' ≁ C''. So in the abstract setting 'unique up to equivalence' (ETT.tex:1948) needs its reading fixed. Whether the generated reading is refutable is open; it would need i₁ not bijective. Over the geometry all readings coincide (isMor_inv). What this shows: the abstract statement fails without a locality hypothesis, because a carrier's causality is not determined by local isomorphisms. Whether a hypothesis such as absolute minimality (which is not a gluing axiom, kb/0014) suffices is open. It says nothing about the paper's singular flat spacetimes, where the statement holds over the geometry (ett_cauchy_pgcd).

statements.scope_notes: No `sorry`. The trichotomy and 'only the last case obstructs' are proved; the last sentence is false for the literal C (which contains the graph) and proved for the pairs with distinct images (Gluing.Cdist). WP-4, audited.

statements.blocked_on: OQ-14: the set C of rem:non_separe_cas
paper_findings: ETT.tex:2011 C is defined as the pairs (p,q) ∈ M1×M2 with π(p), π(q) not separated. Two equal points are never separated, so C contains every (j₁(x), j₂(x)) (Gluing.graph_subset_C) and C ≠ ∅ as soon as N ≠ ∅, even when the quotient is Hausdorff (Gluing.t2Space_and_C_nonempty). The last sentence of rem:non_separe_cas ('it is the case C ≠ ∅') is therefore false as written, and so is prop:Cauchy_point_min's hypothesis 'C ≠ ∅' in its literal reading. Every use of C (lem:corresponding_K, cor:model_corresponding, prop:C_connexe 'C is closed', prop:Cauchy_point_min, proof of prop:ppcm_Cauchy at l.2320-2324) needs the pairs with DISTINCT non-separated images. Suggest: add 'distinct' (or π(p) ≠ π(q)) to the definition of C. With that reading (Gluing.Cdist) the remark is proved: Cdist = closure(graph) ∖ graph ⊆ ∂j₁(N) × ∂j₂(N), and the quotient is Hausdorff iff Cdist = ∅.

The literal C is exactly the closure in M1×M2 of the graph {(j₁(x), j₂(x))} (Gluing.C_eq_closure, no separation axiom): this is the neighbourhood form of the sentence 'a sequence (a_n) with j₁(a_n) → p and j₂(a_n) → q exists because π(p) and π(q) are not separated' in the proof of lem:corresponding_K (l.2111). A cleaner statement of the whole remark: the gluing is Hausdorff iff M1, M2 are and the graph of f = j₂∘j₁⁻¹ is closed in M1×M2 (Gluing.t2Space_iff).

The remark is a necessary condition only: a pair in ∂j₁(N)×∂j₂(N) need not be non-separated; 'only the last case obstructs' is proved as: for Hausdorff M1, M2 the quotient is Hausdorff iff every pair of ∂j₁(N)×∂j₂(N) has separated images (Gluing.t2Space_iff_frontier). The line with two origins (two copies of ℝ glued along ℝ∖{0}) is the example: (0,0) ∈ Cdist and the gluing is not Hausdorff.

paper_findings: Minor, aimed at the EDITORIAL proof ('[editorial] supplied 2026-08-22 -- verify', l.2068), not the author's: an omitted standard step. ETT.tex:2071-2074 concatenates a causal curve from σ to ψ(x,t) with the flow segment and invokes the Cauchy property, but a Cauchy surface constrains inextensible causal curves only (DEC-14), so the finite concatenated curve must first be extended to an inextensible one (existence of inextensible extensions, standard in the Lorentzian setting); the curve from σ to ψ(x,t) also uses causal arc-connectedness. What is used is the acausality of Σ.

lem:Sigma_separe (l.2062) is stated after lem:image_diamant (l.2024), whose proof uses its consequence M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ). T-ett-sigma-separe: the cover M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ) needs neither ψ nor causality (Causal.Causality.IsCauchySurface.cover_of_t1_secondCountable, T1 and second countable), so the « In particular » can be stated as its own lemma before lem:image_diamant (l.2024).

ETT.tex:2067–2068 (T-ett-sigma-separe): the proof of the « In particular » needs neither ψ nor global hyperbolicity: causality, Hausdorffness, Z⁺ = M, chronology at the points of Σ and the BTZ lines suffice, and the time-reversed neighbourhood fact, the cover M = J⁺(Σ) ∪ J⁻(Σ) and the closedness of Σ hold too (Causal.Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.sigma_separe_of_isCausal; at E≥0-manifolds, Causal.SingularRowsCauchy.sigma_separe_of_isCausal). So it does not depend on lem:vecteur, on theo:geroch_sing's splitting or on compact diamonds. The gain is in the route, not in the class of spacetimes: by theo:geroch_sing (iii)⇒(i) (l.1771–1777) a singular flat spacetime with a Cauchy surface is globally hyperbolic in the paper (in Lean that direction is OQ-32's tagged sorry, so the causal-only form is the one proved without it).

ETT.tex:2071–2080 (the editorial proof), for a ψ-free rewrite (T-ett-sigma-separe): at a BTZ point p ∈ J⁺(Σ) ∖ Σ, I⁻(p) = ∅, so no q ≪ p gives an open I⁺(q) ⊆ J⁺(Σ); the neighbourhood comes from tarentin and the BTZ half-line J⁻(p) = γ(]−∞,0]), which meets Σ at γ(s₀), s₀ < 0, giving a = γ(t), s₀ < t ≤ 0, with p ∈ Int J⁺(a) ⊆ J⁺(Σ) ∖ Σ. The case cannot be avoided: every Cauchy surface of a causal singular flat spacetime with sing₀ ≠ ∅ has BTZ points in J⁺(Σ) ∖ Σ (Causal.Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.exists_mem_sing_zero_Jplus_diff).

ETT.tex:2062–2064 against l.1778–1795 (T-ett-geroch-split-flow): lem:Sigma_separe takes ψ from theo:geroch_sing, but topologically the dependency runs the other way: the « Moreover »'s ψ is a homeomorphism because J^±(Σ) are closed, which is the ψ-free « In particular ». The equalities need neither global hyperbolicity nor a homeomorphism: acausality of Σ replaces the editorial proof's concatenated curve (l.2075–2077) (Causal.Causality.IsCausalFlow.Jplus_eq_image). For singular flat spacetimes the gain is in the route, not the class (by (iii)⇒(i) a spacetime with a Cauchy surface is globally hyperbolic in the paper).
